title: The Primacy Bias in Deep Reinforcement Learning
mechanism: Early experience/high replay can impair subsequent learning.
intervention: Periodic network resets while retaining replay buffer.
diagnostic: Priming experiments; buffer and optimizer ablations.
limitations: Reset benefit does not uniquely identify a root cause; later occupancy changes.
relevance: Same accumulated data, different learner states; essential buffer-preservation control.

title: Revisiting Plasticity in Visual Reinforcement Learning: Data, Modules and Training Stages
mechanism: Augmentation and critic activity interact with training stage and replay ratio.
intervention: Critic-FAU rule switches low replay ratio to high.
diagnostic: Fraction of Active Units and change between checkpoints.
limitations: Single-knob hand-designed rule; FAU is a proxy, not isolated trainability.
relevance: Direct prior for diagnostics→adaptive intervention; factorial data×reset experiment.

title: Dissecting Deep RL with High Update Ratios: Combatting Value Divergence
mechanism: OOD action prediction and Adam momentum can amplify Q-value divergence.
intervention: Output-feature/unit-ball normalization; actor and critic reset ablations.
diagnostic: Q-values, priming, optimizer and actor comparisons.
limitations: Additional actor/exploration effects remain; does not identify a universal cause.
relevance: Weights/optimizer/targets/occupancy explanations can interact under high UTD.

title: ROER: Regularized Optimal Experience Replay
mechanism: Links replay prioritization to regularized occupancy optimization.
intervention: TD-error-derived replay reweighting with KL-divergence regularization.
diagnostic: TD error/occupancy ratios; no plasticity diagnosis.
limitations: Not a repair selector; priorities depend on learner and targets.
relevance: Concrete data-distribution intervention; distinguishes effective sampling from collection.

title: Non-Stationary Learning of Neural Networks with Automatic Soft Parameter Reset
mechanism: Learned OU drift models changing parameters/non-stationarity.
intervention: Adaptive soft reset plus learning-rate adjustment.
diagnostic: Predictive likelihood optimized on data; fresh chunks in SAC.
limitations: One intervention family; RL Hopper/Humanoid with three seeds; higher Bayesian compute.
relevance: Strong prior for learning when/how strongly to intervene from data.
code_status: No release claimed: paper checklist cites IP constraints.

title: Self-Normalized Resets for Plasticity in Continual Learning
mechanism: Detects inactive neurons via history of inter-firing times.
intervention: Neuron reset after rejection of positive firing-rate hypothesis.
limitations: Predominantly supervised continual-learning evaluation; single reset family.
relevance: Prior for statistically motivated diagnostic and adaptive reset timing.

title: Preserving Plasticity in Continual Learning with Adaptive Linearity Injection
intervention: Learned per-neuron linearity injection with derivative-based gate.
limitations: Continuous activation intervention; RL evidence checked in arXiv v1 only.
relevance: Adaptive plasticity preservation baseline, distinct from discrete repair selection.
metadata_note: arXiv says accepted CoLLAs 2025; current PMLR labels proceedings 2026. Preserve version distinction.

title: Silent Neuron Theory and Plasticity Preservation for Deep Reinforcement Learning in Adaptive Video Streaming
mechanism: Forward inactivity alone need not imply impaired backward learning.
intervention: Selective perturbation/reset of neurons with low forward and backward activity.
limitations: Domain-specific adaptive video streaming; assumptions in theoretical tracking analysis.
relevance: Shows why dormancy alone is an unreliable causal label; targeted diagnostic repair.
metadata_note: Original 2025 title: Understanding and Exploiting Plasticity for Non-stationary Network Resource Adaptation.

title: Calibrated Partial Resets: Preventing Policy Collapse in Continual Reinforcement Learning
mechanism: Binary resets may destabilize long-horizon continual RL.
diagnostic: Layer-normalized EMA of incoming-weight gradient magnitude.
limitations: Designed utility→intensity mapping with tunable reset fraction; no heterogeneous repair selector.
relevance: Fresh direct prior for selecting how strongly to repair from measured state.

title: NeuMoSync: End-to-End Neuromodulatory Control for Plasticity and Adaptability in Continual Learning
mechanism: Global learned modulation coordinates activity and plasticity.
diagnostic: Current input plus neuron position, learned features and activation history.
limitations: Supervised CL benchmarks; not discrete RL checkpoint repair selection.
relevance: Closest learned-control prior; snapshot-copy fixed-budget adaptation evaluation overlaps protocol.
